Plot the acceptance checks of a calibration

Source: R/visuals_calibration.R
plot.pdm_calibration_checks.Rd

plot() and autoplot() draw the checks of calibration_checks():

Usage

# S3 method for class 'pdm_calibration_checks'
plot(x, type = c("bounds", "peaks", "timing", "balance"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'pdm_calibration_checks'
autoplot(object, type = c("bounds", "peaks", "timing", "balance"), ...)

Arguments

x, object

A result of calibration_checks().

type

One of the plots above.

...

Passed to plot.pdm_events() for the event plots.

Value

plot(): x, invisibly. autoplot(): a ggplot.

Details

typeShows
boundswhere each parameter sits within its search range; one at an end is flagged
peaks, timing, balancethe project's events by window, as plot.pdm_events() draws

A parameter at an end of its range is the clearest warning sign a calibration gives: the search wanted to go further than a sensible value, usually to make up for something the structure cannot do.

See also

calibration_checks(), plot.pdm_events()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
checks <- calibration_checks("projects/beggearn_huish")
plot(checks)
plot(checks, type = "peaks")
} # }
